questions.stem: Why can membership inference be harmful even without extracting the record's content?
options: Confirming someone was in a dataset (for example, a clinic's patients) can itself reveal sensitive facts
questions.explain: Membership itself can be sensitive.

questions.stem: What is the main risk of treating stored embeddings as anonymised data?
options: Inversion can reconstruct much of the original text from vectors
Embeddings take too much disk space
questions.explain: OWASP LLM08 warns embeddings can leak source text via inversion (T0024.001).

questions.stem: Which TWO controls reduce membership-inference and extraction risk? (Select TWO)
options: Allow unauthenticated access to the vector store
Limit output detail, such as not returning raw confidence scores
questions.explain: Less output detail and rate limits make inference harder. The other options increase risk.

questions.stem: Which technique trains with calibrated noise so no single record measurably changes the model?
questions.explain: Differential privacy limits what can be inferred about any one record.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

statements.s: Access control on the vector store matters as much as on the source documents
ATLAS AML.M0019 covers controlling access to AI models and data in production
Embedding inversion requires physical access to the GPU

questions.explain: Vectors can leak their source text, so protect them. M0019 is production access control. Inversion works from vectors or outputs.

questions.stem: Which ATLAS mitigation is Control Access to AI Models and Data at Rest?
questions.explain: M0005 covers data at rest; M0019 covers production access.

questions.stem: Order the ingestion pipeline controls as a document flows into the index.
options: Sanitise to plain text and strip hidden content
Scan for instruction-like text and secrets
Tag chunks with provenance and hash
questions.explain: Check the source, clean, scan, tag, then index with versioning.

questions.stem: Which ATLAS mitigation is Sanitize Training Data?
questions.explain: Sanitize Training Data is M0007.

questions.stem: Why record source, author, timestamp and hash on every chunk?
options: So poisoned or leaked content can be traced to its origin and removed quickly
questions.explain: Provenance enables investigation and targeted removal.

questions.stem: Which TWO ingestion controls most directly reduce poisoning via hidden content? (Select TWO)
options: Convert documents to plain text and drop hidden formatting
Scan for instruction-like language addressed to AI
questions.explain: Sanitisation and scanning catch hidden and instruction-like content.

questions.stem: Complete the ingestion step so each chunk carries provenance metadata.
questions.explain: A content hash lets you verify integrity and find identical poisoned chunks. Random values, lengths and titles don't identify content.

questions.stem: Complete the ingestion filter so documents from unapproved sources are rejected.
questions.explain: Quarantine anything whose host isn't approved.

questions.stem: For each ingestion practice, select Yes if it is good practice.

statements.s: Holding content from lower-trust sources in quarantine for review
Indexing secrets so the bot can help admins faster
Keeping an ML-BOM listing the indexed sources and models

questions.explain: Quarantine and ML-BOMs help; secrets must never be indexed.

questions.stem: What is security trimming in a RAG system?
options: Removing results the asking user lacks permission to see, at query time
Deleting old documents to save space
questions.explain: Security trimming filters retrieval by the user's permissions.

questions.stem: Where should document-level access control be enforced to prevent RAG disclosure?
options: Inside the retrieval query, using ACL metadata on each chunk and the user's identity
Only in the final answer text
Only in the model's system prompt
questions.explain: Restricted chunks must never become candidates for the prompt.

questions.stem: Why should the retriever use the user's identity or a delegated token rather than a super-user service account?
options: So results are limited to what that user can already access
questions.explain: A super-user retriever ignores per-user permissions and maximises exposure.

questions.stem: Complete the vector search so results are limited to the user's groups.
questions.explain: Filtering on the user's groups enforces document-level access at query time.

questions.stem: Which TWO practices keep retrieval-time access control correct over time? (Select TWO)
options: Partition highly sensitive data into separate indexes
Sync chunk ACLs when source permissions change
Copy all documents into one public index
questions.explain: ACLs must stay in sync, and high-risk data benefits from separation.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

statements.s: Microsoft 365 Copilot grounds answers only on content the user already has permission to access
Filtering the final answer is equivalent to filtering the retrieval query
ATLAS AML.M0019 relates to controlling access to AI data in production

questions.explain: Copilot respects existing permissions; output filtering is not equivalent; M0019 is production access control.

questions.stem: Case: after adding a group filter to the vector query, a red-team retest still extracts HR data. What should the assessor check next?
options: Whether HR chunks carry correct ACL metadata and whether a cache or second index bypasses the filter
Whether the UI uses dark mode
Whether the model is large enough
questions.explain: Missing or stale ACL tags, caches and secondary indexes are common bypasses.

questions.stem: Which control is the LAST line of defence for PII appearing in a RAG answer?
options: Output redaction of PII before display
questions.explain: Redaction on output is the final layer; the others act earlier.

questions.stem: One account sends 3,000 near-duplicate questions in an hour to a RAG bot. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Treat it as possible systematic extraction: rate-limit, alert and investigate
questions.explain: High-volume probing suggests extraction or inference; rate limits and investigation follow.

questions.stem: Why should retrieval logs be immutable or tamper-evident?
options: So investigators can trust which chunks produced which answers, even if an attacker gains access
questions.explain: OWASP LLM08 recommends immutable logs for investigation.

questions.stem: Which TWO checks help detect poisoned answers on critical topics? (Select TWO)
options: Alert when answers change right after a document edit
Compare answers against the system of record (grounding checks)
questions.explain: Grounding checks and change-correlated alerts reveal poisoning.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

statements.s: Output redaction should be the only RAG control
Rate limits slow systematic extraction and inference attacks
Periodic re-scans of the corpus can find poisoned content added after ingestion checks

questions.explain: Redaction is a last layer; rate limits and re-scans add depth.

questions.stem: Complete the output step so detected PII is masked before display.
questions.code:
answer = generate(question, chunks)
for entity in pii_detector(answer):
    answer = answer.replace(entity.text, ____)
return answer
questions.explain: Replacing with a placeholder masks the value visibly; the empty string can garble meaning, and the others still leak the data.

questions.stem: Which ATLAS mitigation is Generative AI Guardrails, which includes output redaction?
questions.explain: M0020 is Generative AI Guardrails.

questions.stem: In a RAG defence write-up, which control best answers a cross-department data disclosure finding?
options: Document-level ACLs carried into chunks and enforced in the retrieval query
questions.explain: Disclosure is fixed at retrieval with access control.

questions.stem: Which control best answers a RAG poisoning finding from a publicly editable wiki?
options: Restrict indexed sources and add sanitisation, scanning and provenance at ingestion
questions.explain: Poisoning is addressed at ingestion.

questions.stem: Order the layers of RAG defence in depth from earliest to latest in the data flow.
questions.explain: Stop bad content entering, restrict what each user can retrieve, filter outputs, then watch and retest.

questions.stem: Which TWO make a RAG-defence recommendation strong for the AI1 written deliverable? (Select TWO)
options: Each control has an owner and a verification or retest step
Each control is tied to a specific finding and an OWASP/ATLAS reference
questions.explain: Specific, mapped, owned and verifiable controls score well.

questions.stem: For each pairing of finding and control, select Yes if it is appropriate.

statements.s: RAG poisoning → source allow-listing and provenance (AML.M0025)
Cross-tenant leakage → per-tenant partitioning and query-time filters
Credential harvesting via RAG → raise the model's temperature

questions.explain: The first two match their layers; temperature has nothing to do with indexed secrets.

questions.stem: A report lists: (A) query-time ACL filter, (B) output PII redaction, (C) 'remind the model about confidentiality'. Disclosure is the top risk. What is the best priority order?
questions.explain: Remove the root cause first (A), add a last layer (B); prompt reminders are weakest.

questions.stem: Which RAG stage does an attacker who edits a source document affect first?
questions.explain: The edited document enters at ingestion and is then chunked, embedded and retrievable.

questions.stem: Which OWASP LLM08 recommendation directly addresses multi-tenant RAG?
options: Permission-aware vector stores with logical partitioning
questions.explain: OWASP LLM08 recommends permission-aware stores and partitioning by access level.

questions.stem: Case: a legal firm's assistant indexes all matter files in one store and answers any lawyer's question. A junior associate retrieves memos from a matter they're walled off from. Which TWO controls address the root cause? (Select TWO)
options: Run the retriever with the asking lawyer's identity
Add 'respect ethical walls' to the system prompt
Carry matter-level ethical-wall ACLs into chunks and filter retrieval by them
questions.explain: Permission metadata plus user-identity retrieval stops walled-off chunks from being retrieved; prompt text and model size don't.

questions.stem: Which content pattern most suggests keyword stuffing for relevance hijacking?
options: An FAQ with one topic per question
A long policy with clear headings
A short page repeating many unrelated popular query terms
questions.explain: Stuffing many unrelated terms makes content match many queries.

questions.stem: Case: a hospital wants a RAG assistant over clinical guidelines and staff-uploaded notes. Which ingestion design is safest?
options: Index only approved guideline repositories; quarantine staff uploads for review, sanitise and tag provenance before indexing
Index all uploads immediately to keep answers fresh
Let the model decide which uploads to trust
questions.explain: Separate trusted sources from user uploads and gate the latter.

questions.stem: Case: a clinic exposes a symptom-checker model with an API returning full probability scores, unauthenticated and without rate limits. For each statement, select Yes if it is a valid finding.

statements.s: Membership inference risk is elevated by detailed confidence scores
Missing rate limits make systematic probing cheap
The main fix is adding a friendlier disclaimer

questions.explain: Rich outputs and unlimited queries enable inference; disclaimers don't reduce it. Fixes: authentication, rate limits, reduced output detail.

questions.stem: Which ATLAS mitigation most directly supports investigating which chunks produced a harmful answer?
options: AML.M0029 Human In-the-Loop for AI Agent Actions
questions.explain: Telemetry logging records retrievals and responses for investigation.
